title: A User-Centric Exploration of Axiomatic Explainable AI in Participatory Budgeting
authors: Hashemi, M.; Darejeh, A.; Cruz, F.
tldr: Axiomatic explanations in participatory budgeting improve user understanding and perceived fairness, though trust effects are inconclusive.
problem_and_motivation: Participatory budgeting mechanisms aim to allocate funds based on votes and budget constraints, but lack transparency in decision-making. Users often do not understand why certain projects are funded while others are not. There is a need for explainable approaches that enhance transparency and trust in budget allocation systems.
approach: Proposed an axiomatic approach treating budget allocation as constraint-solving with linear constraints.
Formulated feasibility, exhaustiveness, and utilitarian welfare axioms as integer linear programming constraints.
Evaluated approach through user study with 26 participants using two participatory budgeting scenarios.
Compared understanding, trust, and perceived fairness before and after receiving explanations.
Analyzed user preferences between general and counterfactual explanation types.
findings: num: 72.4% of participants found explanations extremely or very helpful for understanding.
num: 63.3% preferred general explanations over counterfactual ones.
num: 30% reported positive impact on perceived fairness after explanations.
num: 27% increased trust, 23% decreased trust, 50% unchanged after explanations.
num: User understanding and perceived fairness improved in both test cases.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper contributes an axiomatic approach to providing transparent explanations in participatory budgeting decisions. It formulates budget allocation axioms as integer linear programming constraints for systematic outcome verification. The work evaluates explanation effectiveness through real-world user studies measuring understanding, trust, and fairness perceptions. Findings indicate explanations improve user understanding and perceived fairness, though trust effects are mixed.
directly_justifies: Axiomatic explanations treat budget allocation as constraint-solving problem.
72.4% of users found axiomatic explanations helpful for understanding.
Users prefer general explanations over counterfactual ones in budgeting contexts.
limits: Small pilot study with only 26 participants.
Mixed results on trust improvement from explanations.
Limited to approval voting and non-divisible project settings.
No evaluation of computational scalability for larger budgets.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan of all topic domains identified high relevance for budgeting strategies (7.A) due to core focus on participatory budgeting axioms and allocation mechanisms. Medium relevance for budget recommendation (7.B), user trust (10.B), and evaluation frameworks (12.A) as supporting aspects. Low relevance for landscape of existing systems (4.A) and engagement dynamics (11.A) as contextual background. Domains related to Filipino demographics, expense categorization, predictive modeling, and anomaly detection were considered and rejected as not covered by this explainable AI budgeting paper.
